slot_note: seed DQ08 (which reporting areas get a completeness alert while recent weeks are still filling in): the decision (which reporting units get a completeness alert in this run) and the quantity (what has arrived against what should have by now) kept; the world moves from disease surveillance to a mobile game studio's purchase tracking, because Epidemiology x Data Quality is banned against task234 and because a build's tracking loss is a measurement quantity of product analytics that no other field has
niche: a mobile game studio's weekly tracking-quality run deciding which iOS and Android builds of its puzzle game get a purchase-tracking-loss alert, judged on the share of each build's store-verified purchases whose client purchase event never reaches the warehouse, in a week when the newest build is mid-rollout on a new analytics SDK and casual players on old builds come back only weekly
stakeholder_role: data quality lead in a mobile game studio's analytics team, who runs the weekly tracking-quality check on the game's production builds

spine.entity: one session start the game's backend recorded for a device that bought in the window

world.geography: Ireland (a Dublin game studio; players worldwide; personas on the en_IE index)

driver: An item missing from a source's feed is lost only once its sending device has had its next chance to send it, a chance a separate real-time log records device by device; the loss rate has to be read among items whose device has made contact since, while a settle window counts a slow sender's waiting items as lost and cannot judge a source too new to settle, and reading the chance at the account instead of the device grants chances that never came.
driver_concrete: A purchase event the game's analytics SDK could not send before the player left the game waits on that phone until the phone next opens the game, which the backend's session log records the moment it happens; a build's tracking loss is the share of its purchases without an event among purchases whose phone has opened the game since, so iOS 7.42.0 on the new SDK and Android 7.41.0 lose 4 and 6 per cent, while a seven-day settle window charges the weekly players' waiting events on the 7.38 and 7.39 builds as losses and leaves 7.42.0 unjudged.
stump: A competent solver counts a purchase as lost when its event has not arrived seven days after it, alerts Android 7.41.0 and three old builds whose weekly players have not opened the game again (iOS 7.38.2, Android 7.38.1 and 7.39.0) and leaves iOS 7.42.0 unjudged for want of settled purchases; the step that lands it there is treating a missing event as lost before the phone that made the purchase has opened the game again.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who collapses the SDK's duplicate events, drops renewals and sandbox purchases, crosswalks the version strings and reads the window in Irish time, then measures loss over purchases seven days old, files 4 of the 12 builds wrong (three false alerts on old builds, iOS 7.42.0 missed); joining the session log by account instead of by device still files a false alert on iOS 7.41.1.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is a build's purchase-tracking loss, the client-side instrumentation reconciled against the store's server-side purchases with each missing event judged against its phone's next session, the measurement work product analysts do on SDK telemetry; with wards, meters or tills for builds there is no on-device event queue, no session handshake and no store receipt, and the task stops making sense.

differentiation.task234: task234 predicts each source's eventual output from a share in its own current output that a loss cannot move; this build predicts nothing: it identifies purchase by purchase whether the missing event is due yet, from a separate real-time log of the sending phone's next session, and measures loss only over the purchases that are due
differentiation.task231: task231 takes the closed share of silent units from settled rounds the register has caught up with; this build has no settled rounds to borrow from (the newest build is four days old) and judges each missing item by its own sender's next contact, not by a share carried from earlier periods
differentiation.task445: task445 completes a still-open period by imputing each missing reporter's amount from its class's drift; this build imputes no amount: each missing item is classified late or lost by whether its own sending device has made contact since, read from a separate session log, and the loss rate is measured over the items whose device has
differentiation.task459: task459 reads each unit's rate at a committed operating level from interval records instead of its period average; this build has no operating level or rate curve: it decides, item by item, whether a missing record is due yet from its sender's next contact and measures loss only over the items that are

notes: Decisive G12 (a missing purchase event is a non-answer until the phone that made the purchase has opened the game again), G14 supporting (the loss rate conditioned on that delivery chance, pattern E's form), G2 (the chance belongs to the device, not the account). The metrics catalogue files the WHAT (a build's tracking loss: the share of its purchases in the four weeks whose purchase_completed event never reaches the warehouse, purchases whose event can still arrive included; the 2 per cent line) and no method; the SDK notes say the on-device queue survives restarts and name no trigger, which the data show (every late event arrives within a minute of a later session start of its phone). Re-domained from the seed's disease surveillance: Epidemiology x Data Quality is banned against task234.
